sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Shivappa, who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 28-05-2024 at about 3.00 p.m., Shivappa was riding his Bajaj CT100 motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-L-2099 towards his village Mittamalahalli from Kolar and when he reached near Basapura gate, on Kolar-Bethamangla road, Kolar Taluk, at that time KSRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-07-E-1505 came from opposite direction ie., from Bethamangala side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of Shivappa, result of which Shivappa fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, Shivappa was shifted to R.L Jalappa Hospital, Kolar wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he succumbed to the injuries on 03-6-2024 at about 2-45 a.m., during the course of treatment.
3. Prior to the accident, Shivappa was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 41 years.
He was doing coolie work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Due to sudden demise of injured,
petitioners have suffered pain and mental agony and other pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages.

4. The Respondent- the owner cum insurer of the KSRTC bearing No.KA-07-F-1505 has filed written statement and contended that their vehicle was proceeding slowly near Basavapura gate, in front of Byraveshwara Petrol Bunk, at that time the deceased came in a motorcycle from Petrol bunk by riding the two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and without wearing headgear, darted the main road without observing the vehicular movements on the main road and dashed against the right side corner of the bus.

It is categorically submitted by the respondent that the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself and there is no negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.Shivappa, was died on account of road traffic accident took place on 28-05- Manjula vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30563653/
2 2024 about 3-00 p.m., Near Basapura gate, on Kolar-Bethamangala road, Kolar Taluk & District,
due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-07-F-1505?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 and Ex.P10.

On the other hand, the respondent has examined its driver as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
7.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent.
The Learned counsel for respondent has produced memo with 6 rulings.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, Shivappa (herein after called the deceased) was riding his Bajaj CT100 motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-L-2099 towards his village Mittamalahalli from Kolar and when the deceased reached near Basapura gate, on Kolar-Bethamangla road, Kolar Taluk, at that time KSRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA- 07-E-1505 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came from opposite direction ie., from Bethamangala side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of deceased, result of which deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on 03-6-2024 at about 2-45 a.m., during the course of treatment.

10. In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 10 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.8 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, police memo with 2nd complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest Mahazar, PM report, charge sheet are the material documents to prove the present point.

11. On the basis of the complaint lodged by M Ravi, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.0226/2024 of Kolar Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279,
304(A) of IPC.
12.

It is vehemently argued by the Learned counsel for respondent that the petitioner after filling petrol to his vehicle in the petrol bunk has suddenly entered the main road without observing the Manjula vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30563653/
3 vehicular movement on the road and dashed against the alleged offending vehicle on its right side corner.

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel the deceased alone has contributed negligence and submitted that in any event if court comes to the conclusion that the driver of the alleged offending vehicle has also contributed negligence then the percentage of negligence contributed by deceased may be considered on higher side.
13. It is further argued by the Learned counsel that the petitioners being the legal representative of the deceased have to prove the case with all preponderance of probabilities.

The Learned counsel at this juncture has referred judgment reported in (2005) 6 SCC 172 between National Insurance Co.Ltd., vs. Prembai Patel & Ors., wherein it was observed that "the claim petition before the Motor Accident claims tribunal is an action in tort and the injured are the legal representatives of the deceased have to establish by preponderance of probabilities that there was no negligence on the part of the injured or deceased and they were not responsible for the accident".
14.

In (2014) 13 SCC 254 between Lachoo Ram & Ors., Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation, it was observed by referring the facts of the said case that "Simply the involvement of bus in the accident cannot make the respondent liable to pay compensation unless it can be held on the basis of materials on record that the accident was caused by rash and negligent act of the driver".
15.

If the court finds evidence adduced by parties and material placed by parties are sufficient to holds that charge sheet filed by police is a fabricated documents, the claim petition cannot be sustain.
The court do not swayed away by the documents filed u/Sec.173 (5) CPC".

16. In MFA No. 2921/2012 (MV) between Smt. Vijalakshmi K N & Ors., Vs. Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation decided on 09-02-2016, it was observed by referring the facts and evidence of the said case that "the oral evidence itself is not a deciding factor.

sentences.text: In the said case, the sketch clearly disclosed that the cyclist was also wrong to a considerable extent.

Having regard to the manner in which the bus was being driven, it was held that the greater decree of negligence is attributable to the bus driver and accordingly apportioned negligence at an extent of 60:40.
18.
In 2023 (2) ACR 676 between Sanna Papamma Vs. Basavaraj.
In the said case, accident was occurred when deceased was crossing National High way on his moped.
Moreover, he was carrying maize bags on moped.
The deceased without observing traffic rules, without noticing car suddenly crossed the road without taking care and caution and hence accident was occurred.
Hence, the Hon'ble High Court has apportioned the contributory negligence on part of deceased to an extent of 25%.

sentences.text: By referring the aforesaid judgment it is vehemently argued by learned counsel for respondent that even though charge sheet is filed against the driver of the alleged offending vehicle but the said charge sheet is not a conclusive proof and since deceased has contributed grater decree of negligence, the petitioners have to forgo compensation to the extent of negligence contributed by the deceased.

20. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent, if the materials placed on record is perused, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident the deceased was proceeding in his two wheeler from Kolar towards Bethamangala and the offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction i.e., from Bethamangala towards Kolar.

Though the respondent and RW.1 has stated that the deceased by filling fuel to his vehicle in the petrol bunk all of a sudden entered the main road without observing the vehicular movement but none of the documents discloses the said fact of deceased while entering main road from petrol bunk met with an accident.
If the spot mahazar and sketch which has not been disputed by the respondent is carefully perused, as per the said admitted documents the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 20 feet.
If the boundaries of the spot of accident as mentioned in Ex.P3 is perused, near by to the four directions of the scene occurrence there is no any mention of the existence of petrol bunk.
If sketch at Ex.P4 is perused, it is at a long distance from the spot of accident there exist one petrol bunk.

Even if it is taken for the sake of discussion that the deceased by filling fuel to his vehicle in the petrol bunk shown in the Ex.P4 entered the main road, then also it cannot be said that the deceased had hit his vehicle against the offending vehicle because the spot of accident is not in front of the petrol bunk but as observed supra, it is for away from the petrol bunk.
Further admittedly deceased was proceeding from Kolar to Bethamangala and offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction.
The spot of accident as depicted in Ex.P3 and Ex.P4 is on the extreme left side of Kolar- Bethamangala road.
It is at about 3 to 4 feet from the left edge of tar road towards right side.
It means, the driver of the offending vehicle by driving his vehicle on the extreme right side of Bethamangala -Kolar road hit his vehicle against the vehicle of the deceased.
Had the driver of offending vehicle driven his vehicle on the left side of Bethamangala -Kolar road this accident would not have occurred.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, this mishap has occurred.
The respondent has produced the photographs allegedly pertaining to the scene of occurrence.
But the said photographs would no way helpful to the case of respondent and the said photographs would not support the case of respondent.
It is true that the respondent has also lodged complaint regarding the accident by blaming on the deceased as the cause for accident.
It is not made known by the respondent the stage at which the complaint lodged by him is.
None of the rulings cited by the respondent is made applicable to the case in hand.
21. The learned counsel for respondent has argued about the delay in lodging the complaint.
It is true that though the accident in question has occurred on 28-05-2024 but complaint came to be lodged on 30- 05-2024.
The complaint was lodged by the brother of deceased.
In the complaint as well as in the FIR , reason for delay has been stated stating that the complainant and others were engaged in providing treatment to the deceased.

If the cause title of the petition is perused,
petitioner no.1 is the widow, petitioner no.2 and 3 are the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 are the aged parents of the deceased.
Hence, one cannot expect them to lodge the complaint when they are undergoing trauma.

sentences.text: Further soon after the accident the deceased was shifted to the hospital and after taking treatment from 28-05-2024 till 03-06-2024, he breathed his last on 03-06-2024.
Complaint was lodged on 30-05-2024 (ie) during the life time of deceased and accordingly FIR was registered for the offences u/Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
After the death of injured on 03-06-2024 one more complaint was filed regarding the death of deceased as per Ex.P2.
Hence, the petitioners have assigned valid reason for delay in lodging the complaint.
As the petitioners have proved the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident, this court holds above point in the affirmative.
23. Issue no 2:
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 41 years.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced Ex.P9/Aadhaar card of the deceased wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01- 01-1983.
Hence it can be gathered that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 41 years.

24. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing coolie work and thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident in question has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
25.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.

26. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, children, parents, 1/4th of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 2/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

27. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 41 years, 25% should be added towards future prospects.

Manjula vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30563653/
6 28.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, by adding 25% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.20,625/-, out of it if  th is deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.15,469/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.25,98,792/-
(Rs 15,469/- x 14 x 12 =Rs.25,98,792/- ).
29.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, the petitioner no1 has lost her husband, petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father and petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their son.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

30. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
31. The PW.1 has deposed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses for the treatment of deceased.
The petitioners have produced 10 medical bills amounting to Rs.14,018/- as per Ex.P.10.
The learned counsel for respondent has not disputed the genuineness of medical bills.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.14,018/- under the head medical expenses.

32. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs.18,150/-
2 Transportation
and funeral
expenses Rs.18,150/-

3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs.2,42,000/
 parental consortium and filial  consortium  (Rs.48,400x5)
 4 Loss of Dependency Rs.25,98,792/-
 5.

Medical bills Rs. 14,018/-
 Total Rs.28,91,110/-

sentences.text:
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for Rs.28,91,110/-
and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.

33. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the RC owner cum insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered in partly affirmative.
34. Issue No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,91,110/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Ninety One Thousand One Hundred Ten only) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the amount and interest within 2 months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 12,91,110/- Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.5,00,000/- each, Petitioner No.4 and 5 are entitled for Rs.3,00,000/- each.

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1, 4 and 5 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:

Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for Rs.28,91,110/-
and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.

Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered in partly affirmative.
34. Issue No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,91,110/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Ninety One Thousand One Hundred Ten only) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the amount and interest within 2 months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 12,91,110/- Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.5,00,000/- each, Petitioner No.4 and 5 are entitled for Rs.3,00,000/- each.
Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1, 4 and 5 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
